title: Showcase
subtitle: Websites, desktop tools, apps and open-source projects: why they are good and who they fit.

products.name: Cursor
products.tagline: The AI editor that actually reads your codebase
products.overview: A VS Code fork built around one obsession: making AI the main character of coding. It indexes your whole repository, so answers and edits carry real cross-file context; Agent mode runs the terminal and breaks down tasks end to end.
highlights: Whole-repo indexing — every answer comes with project context
Tab completion feels like predicting refactors, often one line ahead of you
Agent runs commands, fixes tests and ships complete changes
VS Code extensions and keybindings work out of the box
products.bestFor: Developers who want AI inside real projects, not just in a chat box.
products.pricing: Free for personal use; Pro around $20/mo

products.name: Perplexity
products.tagline: A search engine that cites its sources
products.overview: Instead of ten blue links, you get a synthesized answer with citations. It fetches live web pages, supports follow-up questions like a conversation, and Pro mode runs multi-step deep research for you.
highlights: Every claim carries a citation you can open and verify
Answers come from the live web, not stale model training data
Conversational follow-ups dig one topic to the bottom
Dedicated modes for academic, finance and local queries
products.bestFor: People who research constantly and care about sources and freshness.
products.pricing: Free core; Pro around $20/mo

products.name: HeyGen
products.tagline: A photo that reads your script, lip-synced in 175 languages
products.overview: No camera needed: pick a stock avatar or build one from your own photo, paste in the script, and you get a talking-head video with matched lip movements. The same video can then be re-voiced into another language with the mouth shapes redrawn — no reshoot. Paid plans run on credits, videos can start from text, an image or a reference clip, and the team tiers add shared seats plus Zapier and n8n integrations.
highlights: Build a custom avatar from your own face and voice, then just edit the script instead of reshooting
Whole-video translation with real lip-sync — 175 languages and dialects on paid plans
Photo straight to a talking Avatar IV; paid plans run 30 minutes per video
Credits are the one currency: monthly, they roll over for a month, and you can buy more
Interactive video, in-video quizzes, branching and SCORM export for training content
Business tier adds a shared workspace, brand kit and Zapier, n8n, Make and HubSpot integrations
products.bestFor: People who ship talking-head and explainer video constantly without wanting to light a studio each time, and teams pushing one video into many language markets.
products.pricing: Free: 3 watermarked videos/mo; Creator $29/mo (600 credits), Pro from $49/mo (1,000 credits), Business $149/mo + $20/seat

products.name: BuildHub
products.tagline: The Vibe Coding field guide — learn the words, then build
products.overview: BuildHub is this very site: high-frequency frontend, backend, product, AI and Git jargon explained in plain language with interactive examples, plus practice, a skill library, prompts and this showcase. Made for people who want to build with AI but keep getting stopped by the vocabulary.
highlights: Every term ships with a live example you can play with on the page
Fully bilingual zh/en site with one-click switching
Skill entries carry verified install commands — read it, run it
Open source end to end: terms and code welcome contributions
products.bestFor: Anyone who was once scared off by jargon yet seriously wants to build things with AI.
products.pricing: Free & open source

products.name: Betterprompt
products.tagline: A prompt marketplace billed per run — the credit cost is on the card before you click
products.overview: A marketplace that sells prompts without handing them over: pick one, fill in a few blanks, choose a model (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok are all listed) and get a result in seconds. You pay per run, not per prompt — every run spends credits, and the card shows the cost up front, so nobody has to buy a prompt they haven't tried. Prompts execute on Betterprompt's own servers: buyers submit inputs and get outputs, never the prompt itself, which is exactly why creators are willing to list their best work. The split is stated in the FAQ — a run costs the model price plus a 10% platform fee and 10% to the creator, and failed runs refund the credits. There's also an agent-skill marketplace built on the same idea: the SKILL.md is open to read, the generation logic stays server-side.
highlights: Pay per run, no upfront purchase: their words are "No $5 upfront for a prompt you haven't tried" — credits are spent per run and refunded when a run fails
The price is explained: model cost + 10% platform fee + 10% creator royalty, estimated from recent real runs on that model

The prompt stays a black box — it runs on Betterprompt's servers, so users only ever see input and output. Bringing your own API key isn't allowed either ("Every prompt runs on our keys"): they'd rather lose those users than leak a creator's prompt
Creators get paid through Stripe: publish once, earn on every run, with a dashboard for revenue, usage and reviews; payouts unlock at $10

Agents install one master skill — npx skills add https://github.com/betterpromptme/skills --skill betterprompt — and use it to search and run skills in the marketplace, each with a readable SKILL.md and the generation logic kept separate
Your inputs never train any model (theirs or their providers'); team features are still in private beta behind teams@betterprompt.me
products.bestFor: People who want to sell the prompts they already wrote as an income stream, and people who'd rather fill in two blanks than learn prompt writing at all.
products.pricing: Free plan: 2,000 credits/month (100/day cap — roughly 15 images or hundreds of text runs); Pro 8 $8/mo for 30,000 credits, Pro 20 $20/mo for 80,000; video generation, watermark-free images and publishing are paid-plan only

products.name: Figma
products.tagline: Design in the browser, collaborate in one shared link
products.overview: Figma pulled professional design out of desktop apps and into the browser: everyone opens the same file, cursors visible, like a collaborative doc. Components, auto layout and prototypes are all there, and Dev Mode lets engineers inspect specs and grab code directly.
highlights: Real-time collaboration with pinned comments — no more final_v9 files
Auto layout and variants think like code, so engineers feel at home
Runs in the browser; teammates need zero setup
A huge community file & plugin ecosystem — icons, illustrations, kits
products.bestFor: Every product team — the designer's native tool, worth opening for engineers too.
products.pricing: Free for individuals; paid seats for teams

products.name: Designkit
products.tagline: The design desk for shop owners — product shot to full listing
products.overview: Meitu's commercial design platform, and it only cares about pictures that sell: cut out the product photo, swap the background, dress an AI model, then generate the whole set of store images and detail pages in one pass. Onward it covers selling videos, AI PPT, logos and posters. Recurring jobs — full image set, detail-page modules, viral-poster remake — ship as one-click skills (the site itself calls this tier AI Agent and Skills), so nothing gets dialled in by hand. AI output is metered in 美豆, the site's own credits.
highlights: Cut-out, background swap and AI try-on run as one chain — no retoucher on standby
Image sets, detail pages and viral remakes are packaged as one-click skills
Membership splits personal from enterprise commercial licence — running a personal one for company work is infringement
AI generation spends beans: 330/month on Standard, 1,000/month on Pro, top-ups sold separately
Beyond statics: selling videos, talking-head ads, AI PPT, logo and poster work in one workspace
Web, iOS and Android; 4.9 stars across 92k ratings on the China App Store
products.bestFor: Shop owners and cross-border sellers who need main images, detail pages and selling videos daily without paying a designer.
products.pricing: Priced in RMB: free tier; Standard ¥30/mo (330 beans), Pro ¥88/mo (1,000 beans); team plans and enterprise licences separate

products.name: Framer
products.tagline: Drag a canvas and it becomes a live website
products.overview: A site builder that grew out of a design tool: what you see on the canvas is the published site, not a mockup. CMS, breakpoints and scroll effects are native. A default choice for indie devs and startups shipping marketing sites.
highlights: What you design is literally what ships — no handoff step
Real, performant websites with CMS and interactions
Breakpoints, scroll effects and component animation, all visual
Import Figma designs to fit existing workflows
products.bestFor: People who want a high-quality site or landing page in a day without writing CSS.
products.pricing: Free tier available; custom domains require a paid plan

products.name: Screen Studio
products.tagline: Screen recordings that look like product ads
products.overview: A macOS recorder that auto-zooms smoothly after your cursor, adds motion blur and polished backgrounds — demo videos with a premium feel, no editing skills required. A case study in turning a tiny tolerated annoyance into a paid product.
highlights: Automatic smooth zoom that follows the cursor — no keyframes
Backgrounds, window shadows and animated captions look good by default
Export at publish quality, skipping After Effects entirely
One-time purchase with a free trial — small-tool business done right
products.bestFor: Indie devs and marketers who ship product demo videos constantly.
products.pricing: From about $89 one-time; free trial

products.name: Appllama
products.tagline: Reverse-engineer the design of the world's best iOS apps
products.overview: A design library of top iOS apps: real screens, onboarding flows and paywalls from 1,200+ successful apps, searchable by pattern. It answers not «is the UI pretty» but «what design makes users pay» — and ships an MCP server so AI assistants can consult great app design directly.
highlights: All real screenshots, organized by flow: onboarding, paywall, upgrade
A rare library focused on revenue-driven design
MCP access lets AI coding assistants reference proven patterns while building
New apps added continuously; Pro stays indie-affordable
products.bestFor: Indie devs and designers building subscription apps who want to see how the top ones actually charge.
products.pricing: Free preview; Pro $10/mo; Team $16/seat

products.name: Bencho
products.tagline: A library of interactive UI blocks you can actually play with
products.overview: Bencho collects dozens of finely crafted micro-interaction components — magnetic select, slide to confirm, liquid toggle, pull to refresh. Every block runs live on the page rather than sitting as a screenshot: try it on the spot, hit Edit to tweak parameters in the workbench, and copy it from the Code pane when you like it. All blocks are MIT-licensed — commercial use, no attribution. Built solo by Lorenzo Cabra, with new blocks every week.
highlights: «Everything is live, not mocked»: play with each block before taking it
Every block ships an Edit workbench and a «Show me how» breakdown
The whole block library is MIT — lift it into shipped products, no credit needed
A solo builder's weekly-updated masterclass in micro-interaction taste
products.bestFor: Developers and designers who want their own UI to feel alive, or who collect micro-interaction inspiration.
products.pricing: Completely free; blocks MIT-licensed

products.name: Linear
products.tagline: The taste-maker among project management tools
products.overview: Blazing keyboard-driven operation, restrained UI and a workflow with opinions baked in — Linear turned issue tracking from an obligatory form into something pleasurable. Many teams study it as a benchmark of software taste.
highlights: Sub-second responses and a full keyboard flow that never blocks thinking
Cycles and Roadmaps encode modern engineering process into the product
Git branch status syncs automatically — code and tasks stay connected
Restraint in UI and motion at textbook level
products.bestFor: Product and engineering teams who care about speed and aesthetic taste.
products.pricing: Free for small teams; paid per member

products.name: Raycast
products.tagline: The second brain for your Mac
products.overview: A Spotlight replacement where one command bar runs everything — window management, clipboard history, QuickLinks — plus an extension store for GitHub, Notion and calendars, and AI commands on any selected text. Hard to go back once adopted.
highlights: One command palette for the whole system, fingers never leave the keyboard
AI always near: ask, translate or rewrite any selected text
Community-built extension store covering the SaaS you use daily
Snippets and window layouts are great products on their own
products.bestFor: Every Mac user chasing keyboard-driven efficiency.
products.pricing: Core features free; Pro is paid

products.name: Buffer
products.tagline: One dashboard to schedule every social account
products.overview: One of the longest-running social schedulers: connect X, LinkedIn, Instagram and more, queue your content, publish everywhere on rhythm, then read the analytics to adjust. For solo creators and small teams, Buffer compresses multi-platform operations into a single calendar view.
highlights: One queue across platforms, publishing rhythm made visible
Built-in analytics show which posts actually worked
Browser extension turns any link into a draft in one click
The free tier is genuinely usable for individuals
products.bestFor: Creators who need steady output without being held hostage by per-platform logins.
products.pricing: Free for individuals; teams pay per channel

products.name: 即创
products.tagline: Douyin's ad-creative pipeline — credits come from ad spend, not from a checkout
products.overview: Ocean Engine (Douyin's advertising platform) built its own creative workbench. The left rail is four jobs: the inspiration gallery shows formats that already performed, finished-video tools generate a spot and spin profitable variants from it, raw-material tools make digital-human presenters, AI video and AI scripts, and an asset library keeps it all organised. It charges credits instead of cash, and credits cannot be bought: every Monday the platform issues a weekly amount sized by your ad spend from the week before, and whatever is older than 30 days disappears. This is a production line for advertisers, not a creation site for everyone.
highlights: Credits are not for sale (the official FAQ answer to "can I buy credits" is: not supported yet). Basic credits arrive every Monday 00:00, calculated as last week's ad spend × a platform coefficient, default starting value 180, with a guaranteed floor and a cap, expiring after 30 days. Verified live on an account: seven consecutive weeks of +180, a 720 balance, and 180 expiring every week.

Costs are per second of finished video and the spread between models is enormous: Seedance 1.0 runs 3–10 credits/sec, 1.5 is 14 (7 on promo), 2.0 is 54 (10), 2.5 is 81 (16); outfit swap 12/sec, background swap 8/sec.

The Agent moved from per-task to per-second billing on 2026-09-22 at a flat 2 credits/sec; after the first preview, the next two script revisions regenerate at 90% off (0.2 credits/sec), the third returns to full price.
Digital-human videos are priced off the script: 0.17 seconds of audio per character, multiplied by the model's 1 or 9 credits/sec. Batch jobs add every script together first.

Credits are pre-deducted and the refund rules are explicit: cancel while queuing and you get all of it back, cancel mid-run and you don't, a platform-side failure refunds in full, and anything still queued after 24 hours auto-fails with a refund. The account centre keeps 90 days of history.

Ad spend also buys your place in the queue — scheduling weighs 30-day cumulative spend and creative ROI, and the rules state outright that asset volume is not the main factor. Credits bind to your UID and are shared across organisations under it, but never transferable.
products.bestFor: E-commerce and gaming teams already buying Douyin traffic through Ocean Engine or Qianchuan and shipping dozens of creatives a week. Without an advertiser account you never get past the login screen, so organic-only creators should look elsewhere.
products.pricing: Nothing to pay and nothing to top up: weekly credits from last week's ad spend (default initial value 180, valid 30 days), AI tasks deduct per second of video, several models on limited-time discount

products.name: Are.na
products.tagline: The private collection library designers hoard
products.overview: No like counts, no algorithmic feed, no ads — only human-curated Channels of connected content. Collecting is treated as a form of thinking here. The community's aesthetic density is extremely high; the closest thing to an internet library.
highlights: No algorithmic feed — everything served was arranged by a human
Channels and objects: collecting itself becomes the output
Very high concentration of designers, artists and writers
A restrained product that resists growth hacks — study what it refuses to do
products.bestFor: Designers, writers and PMs hunting for inspiration while escaping algorithmic feeds.
products.pricing: Free to use; Pro subscription for advanced features

products.name: Radio Garden
products.tagline: Spin the globe and listen to any live radio station on Earth
products.overview: Thousands of live radio streams from around the world, laid onto a 3D globe — listen wherever you rotate to. Technologically simple, but the presentation itself is the product: a masterclass in making data feel magical.
highlights: The 3D globe plus spatial audio is delight in a single spin
Live stations worldwide — the content never repeats
Opens in the browser, nothing to install
Proof that re-presenting the same data can invent a new category
products.bestFor: Builders who want to learn «surprise» from it; everyone else, use it as a bedtime radio.
products.pricing: Free

products.name: AppFlowy
products.tagline: The leading open-source Notion alternative
products.overview: Built with Flutter + Rust, AppFlowy is a collaborative AI workspace where your data stays yours. Documents, Grid/Board/Calendar database views and team spaces all work fully offline; for sync and collaboration you can self-host AppFlowy Cloud or use the managed one.
highlights: Local-first: content lives on your own devices by default
Documents, database views and team spaces cover the core Notion workflows
Fully self-hostable via AppFlowy Cloud — sync without vendor servers
Desktop and mobile clients across all major platforms, usable offline
products.bestFor: People and teams who want Notion's capabilities with real data ownership — and developers studying a large Flutter + Rust codebase.
products.pricing: Core features are free and open source; the managed cloud has paid plans

products.name: beautiful-mermaid
products.tagline: Beautiful SVG diagrams from Mermaid — and ASCII for terminals
products.overview: Built by Craft for its own AI assistant, open-sourced in early 2026 (★11K+ since). It targets the friction people hit with the stock Mermaid renderer: presets that don't look professional, recolouring that means fighting CSS classes, no terminal output, and a heavy dependency tree for a simple diagram. Pure TypeScript, zero DOM dependencies, synchronous rendering — one source of text becomes either an SVG for the UI or an ASCII diagram for a terminal, across six types: flowchart, state, sequence, class, ER and XY chart.
highlights: Two colours are enough: pass only background and foreground and every text level, connector and node stroke is derived with color-mix(); 15 built-in themes, any Shiki (VS Code) theme can be fed straight in, and theme switches go through CSS variables without a re-render
Dual output — vector diagrams in the UI, ASCII / Unicode box drawing in CLIs, from the same source text
Synchronous rendering with no DOM: no await, no flash, drops into a React useMemo; measured 113ms for 100 flowcharts

Two caveats from testing: nodes must sit on separate lines — the README's single-line "graph LR; A --> B" throws outright — and ASCII width is counted in code points, so CJK labels push the box borders out of alignment (Latin text is fine)
Maintenance: the npm package has stayed at 1.1.3 since 2026-02-26 and the last commit landed 2026-05-06 — the feature set looks stable, but don't expect new diagram types soon
products.bestFor: Developers embedding diagrams in their own product, CLI tool or agent output who find the default Mermaid renderer ugly and its theming painful.
products.pricing: MIT, free and open source

products.name: System Prompts
products.tagline: The live system prompts of 38 AI products, one tool per page
products.overview: A reference site that lays out the system prompts actually running behind Cursor, v0, Devin, Claude Code, Windsurf and 33 more tools. The text isn't written here — it mirrors, word for word, the ★144K GitHub repository x1xhlol/system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools. What the site adds is readability: the loose txt, md and json files in the repo's vendor folders become one page per tool, split into versioned sections with an anchor table of contents, the category and the official site at the top. It is fully static HTML — no search box, no copy button, no sign-in. It exists to be read end to end.
highlights: Chinese-team products are in the 38 too: Qoder, Trae (the page labels it "AI IDE by ByteDance") and Z.ai Code ("Chinese AI coding tool"). Measured: the Qoder page has 3 sections — Main Prompt, Quest Action, Quest Design — 58,092 characters in total

Old versions stay on the same page, so you can watch a prompt change: the Cursor page has 7 sections (Agent Prompt v2.0, the 2025-09-03 build, Agent CLI 2025-08-07, v1.2, v1.0, Chat Prompt, and Agent Tools v1.0 as JSON), 160,152 characters between them

Tool definitions come with the prompt: every function name, its description, when to use it and when not to, all in the original wording. Designing tools for your own agent, this is a finished example to copy. The v0 page is System Prompt + Tools (JSON), 81,276 characters

Clean paths make it easy to pull in as corpus: /cursor-system-prompt/, /qoder-system-prompt/ — nothing but JSON-LD runs on the page, so one curl gets the whole text. Measured 12.7KB for the homepage, 140KB+ for a tool page

Maintenance: the upstream repo was last pushed 2026-10-12 and splits into 34 vendor folders at the top level (Anthropic, Google, Open Source prompts and so on); the About page states the content is shown under fair use, trademarks belong to the vendors, and a vendor wanting a page down files an issue upstream
products.bestFor: People writing agent prompts or tool descriptions who want real examples to study, and anyone wondering why a given AI product refuses to budge on something — the answer is usually in its system prompt.
products.pricing: Free, no account; upstream repository is GPL-3.0
